commits.headline: fix(tools): permuter setup accepts a candidate defined through an alias
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
A candidate defines func_X as impl(...) __asm__("func_X") when the source
file already declares func_X with another prototype; permuter_setup.py
refused those (no definition of func_X). base.c now calls the function
func_X and compile.sh renames it back (permuter_compile.py --defname).
Needed for level near-misses whose callers declared the prototype first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(tools): ps2eeas_nops: a macro store after li.s does not need a nop
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
An `li.s $f0,X` followed by `s.s $f0,SYMBOL` was counted as a read of the
FPR right after the mtc1, but outside small data the assembler expands the
store to `lui $at` + `swc1`, so the object has no such pair and the tool
aborted with "object has 0 mtc1 uses; source has 1" (func_L18_002FABE0).
When the counts disagree, retry without symbol stores; counts that already
agreed are unchanged, so nothing that built before changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(overlays): level 18 (Veldin 2): func_L18_002F39F8 exact match
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
Walks the level's moby-id list for the caller's slot and copies the

Two levers, both new here:

- The table address must NOT be MACRO_ADDR. With it, the unsplit macro
  puts the whole address in one register; retail splits the halves and
  the allocator uses the argument register as the scratch for the %hi,
  which is why it first copies the argument elsewhere. Dropping it took
  this from 8 bytes…

Reading it after the qcopy lets it go straight into $a0, which is where
retail loads it -- above both stores, with the counter store falling
into the call's delay…

commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
The Ghidra MCP project holds only the executable, so a level's own code
(the part that replaces main when the level loads) could not be read
there, and the headless server cannot import files.

tools/ghidra_level.py builds a flat image of a level's memory (the
resident executable below 0x15F000 from baserom/SCES_509.16, then the
level's records at their load addresses from baserom/overlays/level_NN/),
imports it into a scratch project inside the running ghidra-ps2-mcp
container with…

commits.author: Lynder063

The one remaining difference was the moby table base: retail loads it with

use in the translation unit, so declaring a 4-byte alias there (and using
it in func_L18_002D80B0 and func_L18_002D8140, whose own accesses sit in
branch delay slots and stay $gp-relative) takes the symbol out…

commits.author: Lynder063

This one was already byte-exact as a candidate but could not share a file
with func_L18_002D8140, because it needs D_L18_00160058 in the assembler's
`lui`/`lw` macro form while that neighbour reaches the same symbol through
$gp. The 4-byte alias at the symbol's first use in the file (previous
commit) settles the size for the whole translation unit, so both forms can
now coexist: the neighbours' accesses sit in branch delay slots and stay

commits.headline: fix(nonmatching): level 18: func_L18_002FDB28 one instruction from exact
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
Three levers (notes in build-sn/try): the while(1)+return form stops the
class constant being hoisted out of the loop, a memory read between the two
stores to flags+0x34 keeps gcc from dropping the first one, and reading the
list entry into a local gives retail's sign test. What is left is a register
copy retail makes before masking the entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: feat(overlays): level 18 (Veldin 2): func_L18_002F2AE0 exact match
commits.author: Lynder063
commits.body:
The last nine bytes were the class check in state 0 reading the moby table
base through an alias declared without MACRO_ADDR: gcc splits that into
%hi/%lo, and the scheduler then put `addiu $t0,$zero,0x630` between the
halves and took a third register for the scratch. Through the file's
MACRO_ADDR spelling the access stays one instruction for the compiler and
the assembler expands it to retail's `lui $a3` / `lw $a3,0x58($a3)` pair,
which nothing can split.
